items.title: Germany arrests 2 Iraqis allegedly tied to Iran-linked terror group
items.summary: German police arrested two Iraqi men alleged to be members of an Iran-linked terrorist organization​ that is said to have targeted U.S., Israeli and Jewish institutions in Europe.
items.t: Germany arrests 2 Iraqis allegedly tied to Iran-linked terror group

items.title: Reporters Without Borders demands suspension of controversial French TV channel CNews
items.summary: Paris-based international press freedom group Reporters Without Borders (RSF) on Thursday called on France's media regulator Arcom to suspend right-wing channel CNews for one month over its failure to uphold pluralism. The news channel owned by conservative billionaire Vincent Bolloré condemned the call for its suspension.
items.t: Reporters Without Borders demands suspension of controversial French TV channel CNews

items.title: Oil prices inch back up as Iran and the Houthis escalate threats
items.summary: Increased fighting between Iran's Houthi allies and Saudi Arabia and Tehran's unrelenting threats in the Strait of Hormuz appear to be reversing weeks of oil price declines.
items.t: Iran denounces U.S. use of AI during war

items.title: What would happen if Russia detonated a nuclear weapon in space?
items.summary:
⁠Sputnik-S, a nuclear-enabled satellite, has been assembled by Russia and could be launched in 60 days, reports say

Russia is reportedly preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite into space later this year, in a scenario that could pose a significant threat to global communications.

German media outlets have reported, citing western intelligence agency assessments, that such a satellite could be launched within 60 days and would be operational shortly afterwards.

Continue reading...
items.t: What would happen if Russia detonated a nuclear weapon in space?

items.title: EU leaders wrestle over Ukraine aid as potential Le Pen victory sparks fear
items.summary:
Slovakia, Hungary and Czechia want to opt out of €45bn Ukraine loan, as Germany tries to protect funding from possible far-right French presidency

  • Europe live – latest updates

EU leaders were bracing for a clash over long-term financial aid for Ukraine amid an effort to finalise high-stakes budget talks by the end of the year.

Arriving in Brussels on Thursday, the German chancellor, Friedrich Merz, reiterated his view that all EU member states should support a €45bn (£38bn) loan for Ukraine for 2027. “When the European Union provides funding, it does so as the European Union – and that union consists of 27 member states, not 23 or 24,” he said.

Continue reading...
items.t: EU leaders braced for clashes over Ukraine aid at budget talks

items.title: Spain’s Pablo Hernández de Cos wins race to be next ECB president
items.summary:
Former Bank of Spain governor chosen to succeed Christine Lagarde after winning support of EU’s biggest countries

Spain’s Pablo Hernández de Cos has been chosen as the next president of the European Central Bank, to succeed Christine Lagarde, after winning support from the EU’s biggest countries.

The economist and monetary policymaker will become the first Spaniard to lead the ECB, defeating his rival candidate Klaas Knot, the former head of the Dutch central bank.

Continue reading...
items.t: Spain’s Pablo Hernández de Cos wins race to be next ECB president

items.title: Saudi pop music is thriving — but for the right reasons?
items.summary: As part of Vision 2030, Saudi Arabia's music scene has evolved hugely thanks to state funding and support. Local musicians and DJs are optimistic. But are they actually just helping prop up an authoritarian state?
items.t: Saudi pop music is thriving — but for the right reasons?

items.title: UK bill to implement EU deal will allow ministers to enact closer ties in future
items.summary:
Further deals can be enacted via same legislation, though it excludes rejoining single market, customs union or bloc as a whole

A bill to implement the UK-EU deal will grant significant powers for ministers to enact even closer ties with Brussels, though it will stop short of Labour’s red lines.

The government put what it is calling the “cutting costs bill” before parliament on Thursday, beginning the legislation to put the deal into law after it was agreed with the EU last Friday – though the deal to ease access for food and drink exports will not come into force until 2028, with the emissions trading deal to follow that year.

Continue reading...
items.t: UK bill to implement EU deal will allow ministers to enact closer ties in future

items.title: Will Spain's far right replace Europe's left-wing stalwart?
items.summary: Some 39 million Spaniards will head to the ballot this Sunday to vote in early general elections. Latest polls put the conservative Popular Party ahead of incumbent PM Pedro Sanchez’s Socialists. The third-strongest political force, however, is the far-right Vox party. A strong showing at Sunday’s election could see them form Spain’s next government. FRANCE 24 explains.
items.t: Will Spain's far right replace Europe's left-wing stalwart?

items.title: ACROSS AFRICA: Tunisian Photographer's Family Focus
items.summary: Stories from the continent with Georja Calvin-Smith. This week, health workers struggling to keep pace with DR Congo's Ebola outbreak say they feel abandoned and unsupported. Also, the World Cup was about more than winning... for some fans, at least. Tunisia's performance may not have been all that its supporters had hoped, but sports photographer Hosni Manoubi is far from negative about a family tradition of documenting his country's international sports showings. [Archive Episode, June 2026]
items.t: ACROSS AFRICA: Tunisian Photographer's Family Focus

items.title: Could the Black Sea pull the U.S. into war in Europe?
items.summary: The Russia-Ukraine war is spilling into the Black Sea, where violent incidents have surged, running right up to NATO's doorstep.
items.t: Could the Black Sea pull the U.S. into war in Europe?

items.title: Protests in Iraqi Kurdistan at plans for government in Baghdad to take over oil, border crossings
items.summary: Thousands have gathered in the capital of northern Iraq's semiautonomous Kurdish region, waving flags and voicing opposition to plans for the federal government to take control of oil operations and border crossings.
items.t: Protests in Iraqi Kurdistan at plans for government in Baghdad to take over oil, border crossings

items.title: In California, exceptional tides and nearly 9m-high waves batter the coast
items.summary: USA: Powerful waves and king tides destroyed part of a pier in Pacifica, south of San Francisco, on Wednesday. In Marin County, authorities issued a temporary evacuation order and urged people to stay away from the beach.
items.t: In California, exceptional tides and nearly 9m-high waves batter the coast

items.title: Trump says he wants Putin to ‘pull back all military aggression’ in Europe – as it happened
items.summary:
This blog is now closed

The Danish prime minister, Mette Frederiksen, has acknowledged that leaders remain “very far apart,” agreeing with Germany’s Merz that the current proposal is not going to work.

“The budget is too large and not sufficiently future-oriented,” she said, calling for more work on competitiveness, defence and security.

Continue reading...
items.t: EU leaders brace for tough talks on budget and Ukraine – Europe live

items.title: Spanish economist de Cos to succeed Lagarde as head of ECB
items.summary: Spanish monetary economist Pablo Hernandez de Cos on Thursday was set to replace France's Christine Lagarde as the new head of the European Central Bank (ECB). His nomination comes as the Europe's most powerful financial institution grapples with an Iran war-driven resurgence in inflation and a cost of living crisis.
items.t: Spanish economist de Cos to succeed Lagarde as head of ECB

items.title: Lost homes, stolen freedom: National Book Award winners on exile and imprisonment
items.summary: Two books about losing everything have just won America's most prestigious literary honours. Hannah Lillith Assadi took the National Book Award for fiction for "Paradiso 17", a novel inspired by her late father, who was driven from Palestine in 1948 during the Nakba. Abdelrahman ElGendy won the non-fiction prize for "Huna", his memoir of six years as a political prisoner in Egypt, arrested at 17 alongside his father. ElGendy couldn't be in New York to collect his award: his visa was denied.
items.t: Lost homes, stolen freedom: National Book Award winners on exile and imprisonment

items.title: How far-right Vox is winning over young voters ahead of Spain's snap election
items.summary: Spain's Vox party is winning over many young people ahead of the country's snap election on November 29, particularly men. The far-right party is capitalising on the rising cost of living and anti-immigrant sentiment to expand its once-marginal electoral base.
items.t: How far-right Vox is winning over young voters ahead of Spain's snap election

items.title: Across Africa: The Scars of South Africa's Soweto Uprising
items.summary: 50 years ago, thousands of young South Africans from Soweto protested against apartheid's stranglehold on their education  and the imposition of Afrikaans as a language of instruction. What began as a peaceful protest ended in bloodshed. And men in Northern Benin confront uncomfortable realities about the lives of the women who live and love them.  [Archive edition, June 2026]
items.t: Across Africa: The Scars of South Africa's Soweto Uprising

items.title: Is authoritarian Vietnam ready to phase out the death penalty?
items.summary: Vietnam has voted to abolish the death penalty for six more crimes, continuing a decades-long trend of restricting capital punishment.
items.t: Is authoritarian Vietnam ready to phase out the death penalty?

items.title: Africa's opposition voices face growing pressure
items.summary: Opposition politicians and government critics say arrests, prosecutions and restrictions on public activity are making it harder to challenge those in power. Is a broader pattern emerging?
items.t: Africa's opposition voices face growing pressure

items.title: French actor Gérard Depardieu to stand trial on rape charge
items.summary: A lawyer representing French actor Gérard Depardieu says he has been ordered to stand trial on a charge of raping a young actress at his Paris home in 2018.
items.t: French actor Gérard Depardieu to stand trial on rape charge

items.title: From leadership crises to tech outages, can corporations rebuild public trust?
items.summary: From cyberattacks to network failures to leadership crises, tech corporations are showing signs of vulnerability. The dramatic resignation and return of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has underscored the potential risk of depending on a single leader, both for the company and the entire AI industry. Meanwhile, global outages at Microsoft and a number of US banks have showcased declining public trust in institutions.
items.t: From leadership crises to tech outages, can corporations rebuild public trust?

items.title: French woman on trial for IS group propaganda tells court she’s ‘ashamed’
items.summary: The trial of Émilie König, one of France's most high-profile Islamic State (IS) group recruits, opened in a Paris court on Thursday with the 41-year-old mother of five apologising to her children, mother and the "French nation" for her actions. König travelled in 2012 to Syria, where she appeared in the jihadist group's propaganda videos. She was repatriated to France in 2022.
items.t: French woman on trial for IS group propaganda tells court she’s ‘ashamed’

items.title: FIFA says a cyberattack against it targeted a 'limited set of personal and business information'
items.summary: World football's governing body says the cyberattack targeted personal and business information. They struck at a sensitive time for the under-fire organization and its president, Gianni Infantino.
items.t: FIFA says a cyberattack against it targeted a 'limited set of personal and business information'

items.title: Season's eatings! Celebrating Thanksgiving in France
items.summary: This Thursday marks Thanksgiving in the United States, the biggest travel holiday of the year there and arguably the most important on US calendars. But here in France, it's just another day. However, Americans living in Paris do try to capture the Thanksgiving spirit, though it can be tricky to track down the turkeys and pies required. Joining us to discuss how Americans do Thanksgiving in Paris is Cordon Bleu-trained chef and the owner of Boneshaker Donuts, Amanda Bankert.
items.t: Season's eatings! Celebrating Thanksgiving in France

items.title: Beau Lamarre-Condon used his service weapon to murder two men. Did NSW police recruiters miss any red flags?
items.summary:
Video of convicted double murderer shows him in 2020 deploying a Taser at close range to an Indigenous man’s face, chest and neck

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Beau Lamarre-Condon, the double murderer who killed Jesse Baird and Luke Davies while he was a serving New South Wales police officer, had been under review by the force for repeatedly using his Taser on a man four years before the killings.

On Wednesday, he was convicted after a 12-person jury found he had murdered both men with his police service weapon on 19 February 2024.

Continue reading...
items.t: Beau Lamarre-Condon used his service weapon to murder two men. Did NSW police recruiters miss any red flags?

items.title: Madagascar's near-total abortion ban puts women's lives at risk
items.summary: November 25 marked the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women. Activists argue that tackling gender-based violence also means addressing the wider inequalities that put women at risk, including restrictions on reproductive rights. In Madagascar, abortion is almost entirely banned, even in cases of rape, incest or when a woman's life is at risk. FRANCE 24’s Aurélie Kouman reports on the consequences of the country's strict laws, which force thousands of women to seek unsafe, clandestine procedures.
items.t: Madagascar's near-total abortion ban puts women's lives at risk

items.title: Fighting in eastern Congo forces Ebola workers to evacuate, disrupts outbreak response
items.summary: Escalating fighting in eastern Congo has forced Ebola response workers to leave affected areas and disrupted efforts to contain the deadliest outbreak in the country, health officials and humanitarian workers said Wednesday. Congo’s Ebola outbreak has infected more than 11,700 people and killed more than 5,700 since it was declared in May, according to the latest government data. FRANCE 24's Emmet Livingstone reports from Kinshasa, DR Congo.
items.t: Fighting in eastern Congo forces Ebola workers to evacuate, disrupts outbreak response

items.title: Moscow drone incursions: Poland to create no-fly zone at Ukraine border
items.summary: Poland will soon create a no-fly zone near the Ukrainian border, a deputy defence minister announced on Wednesday, after several incursions into its airspace it blamed on Russia. Poland backs Ukraine as it fights off Russia's near five-year invasion and has repeatedly accused Moscow of seeking to target Kyiv's supporters with drone incursions and other methods.
items.t: Moscow drone incursions: Poland to create no-fly zone at Ukraine border

items.title: Émilie König, 'the muse of the Islamic State group' goes on trial in France
items.summary: French anti-terrorism prosecutors once dubbed her "the muse of the Islamic State group". On Thursday, Émilie König appears before a special criminal court in Paris, seeking to convince judges that she has been deradicalised. Originally from western France, König spent a decade in Syria and is accused of being one of the Islamic State group's most active French propagandists. Charged with criminal association with a terrorist organisation, she maintains that she has no blood on her hands.
items.t: Émilie König, 'the muse of the Islamic State group' goes on trial in France

items.title: Donations to One Nation from two Gina Rinehart associates to be probed by electoral authorities
items.summary:
Exclusive: Australian Electoral Commission to review $1m in donations to Pauline Hanson-led party from Adam Giles and Ian Plimer

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Major donations from close associates of One Nation’s billionaire benefactor, Gina Rinehart, will be reviewed by the Australian Electoral Commission (AEC) amid concerns they were made on behalf of a third party.

The special minister of state, Don Farrell, said on Thursday that information about two $500,000 donations made to the Pauline Hanson-led party could be subject to further regulatory action if they are found not to comply with provisions in the Electoral Act.

Continue reading...
items.t: Donations to One Nation from two Gina Rinehart associates to be probed by electoral authorities

items.title: ‘Disaster’ unfolding as Sydney fire ant outbreak partly blamed on ignored biosecurity recommendations
items.summary:
Farmers’ federation president says Australia ‘can’t even keep [illicit] cigarettes out of the country … let alone some of these difficult-to-detect pests’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Years-old recommendations by Australia’s biosecurity watchdog have been ignored or not acted on by successive federal governments, increasing the risk of an invasive pest outbreak such as the fire ants discovered in Sydney this week, according to experts.

Environmentalists and biosecurity experts warn the large colony of red imported fire ants are a warning sign that the country’s quarantine system is too slow-moving, underfunded and overly concerned with agriculture.

Continue reading...
items.t: ‘Disaster’ unfolding as Sydney fire ant outbreak partly blamed on ignored biosecurity recommendations

items.title: Hugh Jackman not wrong to be ‘concerned’ about Woodside gas project near WA reef, Murray Watt says
items.summary:
Environment minister says he understands concerns about potential impact after 150 scientists and celebrities urged the government to block the project

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

The environment minister, Murray Watt, has acknowledged concerns raised by scientists and celebrity campaigners, including Hugh Jackman, about a contentious Woodside offshore gas proposal in northern Western Australia, saying he “absolutely understands” why they think it could have “very serious impacts” on nature.

The federal government is expected to make a decision on whether to approve the Browse gas development near Scott Reef, about 300km off the Kimberley coast, under national environment law early next year.

Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here

Continue reading...
items.t: Hugh Jackman not wrong to be ‘concerned’ about Woodside gas project near WA reef, Murray Watt says

items.summary:
As the fast-moving outbreak continues to spread in eastern Congo, fighting between rebels and the army is disrupting efforts to contain the spread of the disease.

items.title: Here's why the Black Sea matters for NATO in the Russia-Ukraine war
items.summary: Chris Livesay traveled to Romania to learn about the Black Sea's role in the Russia-Ukraine war, as its Navy works to fend off rogue attacks from Russia targeting Ukraine.
items.t: Here's why the Black Sea matters for NATO in the Russia-Ukraine war

items.title: EU-Indonesia trade deal opens new markets, but challenges remain
items.summary: The agreement offers new export and investment opportunities for Jakarta and Brussels. But can Indonesia turn Europe's growing interest in its markets and critical minerals into sustainable gains at home?
items.t: EU-Indonesia trade deal opens new markets, but challenges remain

items.title: Housing crisis on the ballot: Anger boils over ahead of Spanish election
items.summary: Spaniards head to the polls on Sunday in a general election that was called after street protests for affordable housing. Anger bubbled over after 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal was evicted from her home of seven decades and two decrees to tackle the housing crisis were rejected by parliament. In calling the snap election, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez is hoping the housing issue can galvanise his left-wing base.
items.t: Housing crisis on the ballot: Anger boils over ahead of Spanish election

items.title: 'Europe has two kinds of countries: Small countries & those that haven’t yet realised they’re small’
items.summary: “The implications of having the far right in power in Brussels are enormous,” warns Sophie Pornschlegel, Senior Advisor at the European Policy Centre. With elections approaching in several EU member states, including France and Italy, what would a growing number of far-right, Eurosceptic governments mean for the EU budget, relations between European institutions, common legislation and support for Ukraine? Could Giorgia Meloni could adopt a more radical stance? “The whole idea of the EU is to have a common legislation that is then applied in 27 member states. Otherwise, what is the point of having the EU?”
items.t: 'Europe has two kinds of countries: Small countries & those that haven’t yet realised they’re small’

items.title: North Korea's Kim vows to build more nuclear weapons after ignoring Trump's overture
items.summary:
Leader Kim Jong Un reportedly visited facilities that produce nuclear ingredients and called for building more nuclear weapons to cope with threats from the U.S. and South Korea.

(Image credit: Korean Central News Agency)
items.t: North Korea's Kim vows to build more nuclear weapons after ignoring Trump's overture

items.title: 'As humans we feel spiritually homeless': Turkish author Ece Temelkuran on belonging
items.summary: For Ece Temelkuran, the human condition is "unhomed". Speaking to FRANCE 24, the Turkish author cites the rise of artificial intelligence, climate change and the authoritarian drift as reasons why one may no longer recognise the place one calls home. This feeling of "spiritual homelessness" is something she explores in her latest book, "Nation of Strangers: Rebuilding Home in the 21st Century". Most of all, she highlights the importance of human connection: "In survival mode (...) you live on the kindness of others."
items.t: 'As humans we feel spiritually homeless': Turkish author Ece Temelkuran on belonging

items.title: ‘I’m no longer a UAE official’: UN hopeful Lana Nusseibeh tries to shake off Sudan record
items.summary:
The US and Russia’s candidate for secretary general is on a charm offensive. Can she overcome London’s resistance to her bid?

Lana Nusseibeh is in Britain this week, attempting to present herself as a potential future UN secretary general, and shift the focus from her past as a United Arab Emirates diplomat who denied the country’s role in arming a militia accused of war crimes and genocide in Sudan’s four-year civil war.

It is a high-risk strategy that involves meeting ministers, MPs, academics and holding a public event with the UN Association.

Continue reading...
items.t: ‘I’m no longer a UAE official’: UN hopeful Lana Nusseibeh tries to shake off Sudan record

items.title: Israel threatens to displace one million Palestinians in Gaza unless Hamas disarms
items.summary: Israel's defence minister on Thursday threatened to forcibly displace one million Palestinians in Gaza if Hamas does not move to voluntarily surrender its weapons, as previously promised.
items.t: Israel threatens to displace one million Palestinians in Gaza unless Hamas disarms

items.title: Storms disrupt Thanksgiving travel. And, FCC violated ABC's free speech, judge says
items.summary:
The East Coast's weather is a major concern this holiday, as it could lead to coastal flooding. And, the judge says the FCC can't punish ABC for satire Trump doesn't like.

(Image credit: Timothy A. Clary)
items.t: Storms disrupt Thanksgiving travel. And, FCC violated ABC's free speech, judge says

items.title: Ukraine says it downed a Russian jet-powered drone with a laser
items.summary: Ukraine has used a laser weapon to shoot down a Russian jet-powered drone for the first time, a senior adviser to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says.
items.t: Ukraine says it downed a Russian jet-powered drone with a laser

items.title: China reserves right to take ‘necessary measures’ after Trump’s new tariff proposals
items.summary:
Beijing says new levies amount to ‘political manipulation’, while Brazil ‘will not yield to this type of threat’

  • Trump proposing new tariffs on 14 partners including China and EU

Beijing has said it reserves the right to take “necessary measures” after Donald Trump’s administration proposed new tariffs on goods from China and other major trading partners, triggering a global backlash.

Among the suggested levies on 14 major trading partners announced on Wednesday, China is potentially facing one of the biggest hits. It would face the highest capped rate of 20%, which in some cases will be stacked on top of other import taxes for a total rate of 45%.

Continue reading...
items.t: Trump tariff threat ‘unacceptable’, says Brazil, as China denounces levies as baseless

items.title: Crew member dies after diesel tanker sinks off Ibiza coast
items.summary: Authorities rescued 17 crew members but one later died in hospital after a diesel tanker sank off the Spanish island of Ibiza. A contingency plan against possible pollution damage is now in place.
items.t: Crew member dies after diesel tanker sinks off Ibiza coast

items.title: EU chief urges leaders to 'compromise' for budget deal by year-end
items.summary: European Council President Antonio Costa urged European leaders to seek compromise on the bloc's long-term budget at a summit Thursday, as Brussels pushes to lock in the plans before next year's French election where far-right leader Marine Le Pen is leading in opinion polls. "Now it is time for all of the leaders to participate in this debate with an open mind, a constructive approach, and a sense of compromise. Because we need to approve this budget timely. That means by the end of this year," Costa said. FRANCE 24's Dave Keating reports from Brussels, Belgium.
items.t: EU chief urges leaders to 'compromise' for budget deal by year-end

items.title: French far-right leader Bardella faces fresh anti-Semitism accusations in media reports
items.summary: French far-right leader ⁠Jordan Bardella faced fresh ​accusations of past antisemitic remarks on Thursday, as French media published an additional ​trove of comments purportedly made in chats from when he was a teenager in 2013. The initial allegations against Bardella, the president of the far-right National Rally party, were published ​by investigative outlet ‌Mediapart in September. It reported that he had made ⁠a slew of antisemitic and conspiratorial comments. Bardella denies making antisemitic remarks. FRANCE 24's French Politics Editor Marc Perelman tells us more.
items.t: French far-right leader Bardella faces fresh anti-Semitism accusations in media reports

items.title: Egypt: 31 people killed in Cairo after fuel truck overturns
items.summary: A fire broke out on a busy highway in Egypt’s capital, Cairo, on Wednesday, killing at least 31 people after a fuel truck reportedly overturned. The suspected driver was arrested on Thursday, according to Egypt’s public prosecutor’s office.
items.t: Egypt: 31 people killed in Cairo after fuel truck overturns

items.title: Fuel tanker explosion kills 31 on Egyptian highway
items.summary: A massive fire killed 31 people in Egypt after a speeding driver allegedly crashed into a fuel tanker truck.
items.t: Fuel tanker explosion kills 31 on Egyptian highway

items.title: Older Australians suffering under Labor’s ‘botched’ aged care at home program, inquiry finds
items.summary:
The Support at Home system has ‘baffling’ bureaucracy and ‘rations and denies care’, says Greens chair of Senate inquiry

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Many older Australians are dying before they can access home support, paying exorbitant fees, and being pushed into hospitals and residential care before they are ready because of a flawed federal government aged care program, a Senate inquiry has found.

The inquiry is examining the impact of the Support at Home program, which launched in November 2025 and has been plagued by complaints of making care harder to access and more expensive. The inquiry was due to finish in November, but has been extended for a further year after receiving almost 300 submissions.

Continue reading...
items.t: Older Australians suffering under Labor’s ‘botched’ aged care at home program, inquiry finds

items.title: Russia-Ukraine war extends to the Baltic and the Mediterranean
items.summary: By attacking Russian vessels around the world, Kyiv is trying to up the pressure on Moscow and also sending out signals to its Western allies. What is the impact on global maritime trade?
items.t: Russia-Ukraine war extends to the Baltic and the Mediterranean

items.title: How Chinese companies circumvent chips sanctions in Southeast Asia
items.summary: High-tech AI chips are hard to get in China because of US restrictions. To get around this, Chinese companies often use offshore computing capacity, particularly in Southeast Asia. The US is also trying to stop it.
items.t: How Chinese companies circumvent chips sanctions in Southeast Asia

items.title: Can Rassvet, 'Russia's Starlink' change the course of the war in Ukraine?
items.summary: SpaceX's US Starlink satellite system has played a key role in countering the Russian military in Ukraine, but now a Russian counterpart is under development. What could this mean for Ukraine?
items.t: Can Rassvet, 'Russia's Starlink' change the course of the war in Ukraine?

items.title: ‘Trapped in grief’: wife of Japanese journalist detained by Russia pleads for his release
items.summary:
Yuki Imai being held in Moscow on allegations he conducted ‘espionage’ while working for a newspaper in Sakhalin island in Russia’s far east

The wife of a Japanese journalist who has been detained in Russia for more than a month on suspicion of spying has issued an emotive appeal for his release.

Yuki Imai, a reporter for the Hokkaido Shimbun, was arrested in mid-October as he was preparing to return to Japan from a two-year assignment at the Japanese newspaper’s bureau in the city of Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk, on the island of Sakhalin in Russia’s far east.

Continue reading...
items.t: ‘Trapped in grief’: wife of Japanese journalist detained by Russia pleads for his release

items.title: Thieves steal cufflinks, clock from British royal estate
items.summary: Two Albanian men were accused of breaking into the country home of Prince William and Princess Kate. Holly Williams reports.
items.t: Thieves steal cufflinks, clock from British royal estate

items.title: At least 31 killed as fuel tanker crash ignites large fire on Cairo highway
items.summary:
Blaze on ring road surrounding Egyptian capital injures at least 21 people and leaves cars and motorcycles charred

A crash involving a fuel tanker ignited a huge fire on a highway surrounding Cairo on Wednesday, killing at least 31 people, Egyptian authorities said.

The blaze on the ring road, a key artery that encircles the Egyptian capital, also injured at least 21 people and left more than two dozen cars and motorcycles charred, according to the latest figures released by the health ministry.

Continue reading...
items.t: At least 30 killed as fuel tanker crash ignites large fire on Cairo highway

items.title: Andy Taylor, longtime Duran Duran guitarist, dies at 65
items.summary: Andy Taylor, the original guitarist of the 1980s English new wave band Duran Duran, has died at age 65 following a battle with prostate cancer.

items.summary: Russian government data obtained by pro-Ukraine hackers and analyzed by the BBC indicates that Russia has lost at least 490,334 soldiers during its war on Ukraine.
items.t: Leaked data shows 490,000 Russian forces have died in Ukraine war

items.title: All hostages rescued after Colombian security forces storm supermarket, police say
items.summary:
Unclear if ‘hostage-taker’ who was killed may have been a hostage as daylong siege in Cartagena shopping centre ends

Colombian police have stormed a supermarket in one of the country’s most popular tourist cities, ending a daylong siege in which all the hostages were freed and one man police described as a hostage-taker was killed.

Abelardo de la Espriella, the far-right president, travelled to the Caribbean port city of Cartagena to follow the final hours of negotiations and the tactical assault, in which special forces officers broke through blocked entrances and detonated stun grenades.

Continue reading...
items.t: All hostages rescued after Colombian security forces storm supermarket, says president

items.title: Lululemon founder stuns Canadian women’s leadership conference with sexist comments
items.summary:
Chip Wilson said men importing brides from Thailand was due to women waiting too long to have children

The controversial founder of Lululemon suggested women in Canada are having too few children and this could lead some men to bring in brides from Thailand, in remarks that stunned audience members at a women’s leadership conference.

Chip Wilson, who built the Vancouver yoga-wear startup into a global athleisure empire, was a featured speaker at the Leadership Forum in Calgary earlier this week, an event organized by Axis Connects to advance women in leadership. The organization says it aims to create space for “candid conversations about the barriers women face both in business and society”.

China has flown the first foreign astronaut to its Tiangong space station, starting what it says will be the globalisation of its space operations as the US-led International Space Station (ISS) enters its final years of operation.

Floating through a hatch to enter Tiangong, Pakistan’s Muhammad Zeeshan Ali grinned broadly as he was embraced by the onboard crew in what China’s space agency called the country’s first foreign “space handshake”.

items.summary:
Alain Throo, insurance executive based in London, reportedly gored and later died on hike near Mount Cameroon national park

A Swiss tourist has been killed and British and American tourists have been injured when a group of hikers encountered a herd of elephants in Cameroon.

The group of six tourists, four British, one Swiss and one American, accompanied by local guides, were hiking near the village of Bakingili in the south of the Mount Cameroon national park on 19 November, on a path used by elephants to access a nearby lake, when they encountered the herd of about 15 animals, according to media reports.

items.summary:
Kishanth Peramalya was denied entry due to sexual assault convictions and sent to Africa where he had no connections

The UK sent a Sri Lankan asylum seeker who had been convicted of sexual assault to Eswatini, a southern African country to which he had no connection and where he killed himself.

Kishanth Peramalya was part of a group that set sail from India hoping to reach Canada and claim asylum there. The boat was rescued by the Royal Navy in October 2021 when it got into difficulty and brought to Diego Garcia in the remote British Indian Ocean Territory, which hosts a US-UK military base.

China is misusing Interpol to target and silence dissidents, a leading British lawyer has claimed, as Hong Kong prepares to host the police organisation’s general assembly for the first time.

Ben Keith, a specialist in “red notices” - the Interpol system under which national authorities are requested to locate and detain suspects - said he was working on five cases involving China making questionable requests through Interpol.

Canada is a “sovereign nation” that does not “report” to the United States, the country’s defense minister said after the Pentagon released a scathing memo that criticized the supposedly “atrophied” defence capabilities of its northern neighbour.

The document, released on Tuesday, said Canada had “yet to make the hard decisions and tradeoffs” necessary to meet previous defence spending pledges and become a “credible partner in the defense of our shared continent”.

items.title: More than 300 Russians killed as Moscow props up Mali’s junta, leaked data reveals
items.summary:
Exclusive: Records list 349 deaths in three years in Mali and also shed light on Russia’s military activity elsewhere in Africa

When the attack on Kidal began before dawn on 25 April this year, the Russian fighters were caught off guard. Within the first hour, checkpoints on the outskirts of the remote desert city nestled among the rocky hills of northern Mali had fallen to the insurgents, who pushed towards the police station where fierce fighting erupted.

“Everything was happening at once. Explosions were going off all around us, people were shouting,” recalled a former member of Russia’s Africa Corps who was stationed in Mali at the time and spoke on condition of anonymity. “Nobody knew where the enemy was coming from.”
